summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, diabetes, and pseudoseizures was admitted after an episode of syncope associated with severe abdominal pain radiating to the left testicle, nausea, vomiting, and chest tightness. He had been unable to eat for three days and reported seeing blood and 'soot' in his vomit. In the ED, he had tachycardia and an elevated lactate of 7.2 with an anion gap of 24, which normalized after IV fluids. Workup ruled out myocardial infarction with normal troponins and EKG, and no arrhythmias on telemetry. The syncope was attributed to vagal episodes triggered by pain. He was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, pain control, and antiemetics. By hospital day two, his symptoms improved, he tolerated clear liquids, and was transitioned to oral medications. He was discharged home with improved pain, instructions to restart metformin, new prescription for ondansetron, and follow-up plans.
